title: The Influence of Policy Incentives on Consumers' Purchase of New Energy Vehicles in China: Moderate-Mediate Analysis
content: China is the world’s largest automobile producer, with auto sales in 2024 expected to surpass 31 million units, including 11.5 million new energy vehicles (NEVs). This study examines the impact of government policies on consumers’ willingness to purchase NEVs in four major Chinese cities: Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, and Guangzhou. Using a structural equation model, the research investigates how policy incentives influence purchase intention, focusing on the mediating roles of perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use, as well as the moderating role of test drive experience. The results indicate that government incentives positively affect consumers' perception of NEVs, improving their purchase intention. Test drive experiences also enhance the influence of perceived usefulness and ease of use on purchase intention. The study concludes that effective policy incentives can promote the development of the NEV industry, reduce pollution, support industrial upgrading, and increase consumer satisfaction through improved driving experiences, competitive pricing, and advanced technology, thereby contributing to the sustainable growth of the NEV market in China.
